html:
Minor Cooper Keith was an American businessman who built the railway from San José to the Caribbean port of Limón in Costa Rica, finished in 1890, and planted bananas along it. He helped found the United Fruit Company.

The railway was begun in 1871 with his uncle, the railway builder Henry Meiggs. Swamps and disease killed thousands of workers, many brought from Jamaica and China. To pay for the line, Keith grew bananas beside the track and shipped them to the United States. In return for finishing it, the government of Costa Rica gave him a huge grant of land.

In 1899 his banana business merged into the United Fruit Company, which came to dominate Central America. His railway brought the Afro-Caribbean people of Limón and carried the country's coffee to the Atlantic.
